agree.reason: Starting with traffic, admitting it will get worse, and tying approval to a signal that keeps Alder and 4th at a C speaks directly to the two commissioners' concern, though opposed neighbours may still not be won over.

honest.reason: Every figure and commitment comes from the facts the user supplied, and the speech openly concedes traffic will worsen; the only slight overreach is implying the 412 households stop waiting if it passes, when 64 units can't house them all.

works_the_facts.reason: The numbers are listed as given and never worked: it doesn't say that 64 homes are about one in six of the waiting list, that 72 spaces is more than one per unit, or what 310 trips means per household.

right_comparison.reason: The alternative is put concretely and truthfully: the lot stays an empty parking lot six days a week and the waiting list stays at a three-year wait. No trend is offered, but the brief gave none.

qualification.reason: Making the signal a permit condition is a firm, checkable commitment backed by the study's C rating, but it has no date or stated consequence, and the neighbour-group commitment is open-ended.

objections.reason: Traffic, parking and 20 months of construction trucks are each raised and answered with a specific remedy (the signal condition, the written weekday parking offer, the neighbour group), and it raises no objection the facts already settle.

fit.reason: At about 400 words of plain spoken first-person prose that ends with a clear request, it fits a three-minute public comment.
